business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Clinical Workflow Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (upstream holding jurisdiction; PRC Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise registered in mainland China)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its Supplementary Agreements

Arrangement between the Mainland of the People's Republic of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2007, as amended); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (jointly promulgated by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration of the People's Republic of China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section if destination is a Hague Apostille Convention state; otherwise consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate in the origin state. For mainland China WFOE filing, notarization by a Hong Kong China-Appointed Attesting Officer and certification by the HKSAR High Court. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section for Hague Convention destination states; consular legalization by the PRC diplomatic mission for non-Convention states; for mainland China WFOE filing, China-Appointed Attesting Officer notarization and HKSAR High Court certification. The two foreign-authentication paths are parallel options, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize by a Hong Kong notary public, then either apostille by the HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section for Hague states or consular legalization by PRC Embassy or Consulate for non-Hague states; for mainland China use, CAO notarization plus HKSAR High Court seal. Choose only the path applicable to the destination and never chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy by the Hong Kong Companies Registry; apostille by HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section for Hague Convention destinations; consular legalization by PRC consulate for non-Convention destinations; for mainland China WFOE filings, use the China-Appointed Attesting Officer channel and HKSAR High Court certification. Mutual exclusivity between apostille and consular legalization is preserved.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank under the Hong Kong Banking Ordinance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, followed by apostille by the HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section for Hague Convention destinations or consular legalization by PRC Embassy or Consulate for non-Convention destinations; for mainland China WFOE filings, CAO notarization and HKSAR High Court certification. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Company Secretary or registered agent of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certificate issued and signed by the registered secretary or agent; notarize by a Hong Kong notary public; then apostille by HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section for Hague states or consular legalization by PRC Embassy or Consulate for non-Hague states; for mainland China use, CAO notarization and HKSAR High Court certification. Never chain apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any incorporation filing, conduct risk-based KYC and enhanced due diligence on all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners. Screen against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, HKSAR financial sanctions list, and PRC domestic market entity blacklist and PBOC anti-money laundering monitoring lists. Identify politically exposed persons (PEPs) using a commercial AML database covering domestic and foreign government, legislative, judicial, military, and state-owned-enterprise officials; require senior-management approval for PEP-involved relationships and file suspicious transaction reports with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC) where warranted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Declaration and Registration System, operated through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and municipal market supervision bureaus
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registered in simplified Chinese characters only. A WFOE name must follow the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or operational characteristic, and legal form such as Limited. English names are not separately registrable as the official company name; any English name appears only in bilingual business materials and articles of association. Pinyin may be used as the distinctive element only where it represents the transliteration of the foreign investor's name. Pure Latin-character names and English-only registrations are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days of a name rejection notice from the local market supervision authority, the applicant shall submit a written reconsideration request to the same authority, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed four-tier name composition, and justification for the distinctive element. If the local authority upholds the rejection, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next-higher SAMR authority within 60 days, or institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. Preserve an audit trail of all submissions and receipt stamps.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PRC WFOE engaged in commercial software (ISIC 6201), a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the statutory registered address. SAMR requires an actual verifiable premises within the registered administrative division, evidenced by a lease certificate or title deed, including a room number and postal code. Municipal tax authorities and banks reject mailbox-only addresses because VAT invoicing, payroll registration, medical-data processing, and software service delivery require a physical establishment and supervised record-keeping. A dedicated desk within a licensed co-working space may be tolerated where lease, signage, access, and actual management presence exist, but pure virtual offices create substantial AML and commercial-substance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: On-site inspection risk within the first 12 months is moderate, approximately 25% annual probability for municipal SAMR or tax spot checks, rising materially if the WFOE issues VAT invoices or moves cross-border payments, and falling for fully digital no-revenue entities. Mandatory inspection checklist includes: (1) visible company nameplate at the registered premises; (2) lease agreement in the WFOE name with a term of at least six months; (3) original contract files and EMR software documentation; (4) employment contracts of staff physically present; (5) hardware or cloud-service contracts for the software platform; and (6) books and records supporting VAT reconciliation. The company must maintain a local contact person and original tax registration certificate at the premises at all times.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR company name reservation and registration filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / Municipal Market Supervision Bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee waived; no official charge is levied for initial company registration in mainland China.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign investor corporate document notarization and authentication bundle (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Board Resolution, Articles of Association, Bank Reference Letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong notary public / HKSAR High Court Authentication and Apostille Section / PRC Embassy or Consulate where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Hong Kong market benchmark of HKD 3,000-5,000 per bundle plus courier and legalization fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of all constitutive documents and board resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation service accredited by local SAMR and notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of RMB 80-120 per page, estimated 30 pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure declaration preparation and filing under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional compliance firm / SAMR filing window
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed engagement benchmark of RMB 2,000-3,000 for a single WFOE beneficial owner structure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease deposit and first-year floor-space contribution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental benchmark for a small IT office (approximately 12 square meters in a tier-2 city), representing deposit plus first-year apportioned rent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening support and documentary legalization processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank compliance department / external courier and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank charges are commonly waived; external courier, notarization, and translation fees follow prevailing market benchmarks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Chapter II on Company Establishment and Registration, especially Articles 2, 7, 10, 23, 29, 32, 33, 35, 37, 46, 59 and 68; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 28 and 31; Regulations on Implementing the Foreign Investment Law; Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Articles 58-61 and 68-69; Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law as applied to medical-data-processing entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal or Provincial Market Supervision Administration at the place of the WFOE's registered office, acting as the enterprise registration authority for foreign-invested limited liability companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Application and the Articles of Association, both submitted to the local SAMR-backed Market Supervision Administration; the outcome instrument is the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for statutory WFOE registration under the PRC Company Law. There is no mandatory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a technology and software-service WFOE. The sole shareholder must subscribe to the registered capital stated in the Articles of Association and contribute within the agreed schedule. For the contemplated medical EMR SaaS and internet health information service licensing, the regulator may require evidence of adequate paid-in capital or committed operational funding, although no fixed statutory amount is prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the authorised registered capital of CN_WFOE_LTD is fixed at the sum stated in the Articles of Association, expressed in RMB or the agreed foreign currency, and the sole shareholder's subscription to the said shares is hereby accepted. The Board directs that the issued shares be allotted in accordance with the capital contribution schedule, and that no share capital be reduced or reclassified except by a further shareholders' resolution. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of CN_WFOE_LTD be and is hereby established at the address set out in the Articles of Association, and the legal representative is authorised to execute the lease, to obtain any municipal occupancy certificates and to complete all registered address filings with the State Administration for Market Regulation. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers be and are hereby appointed: [Name] as Executive Director and General Manager and legal representative; [Name] as Supervisor; [Name] as Corporate Secretary and Compliance Officer; and [Name] as Principal Finance Officer. The legal representative shall have authority to execute contracts, filings and licences on behalf of the company, and the finance officer shall have authority to operate bank accounts jointly with the legal representative. RESOLVED, that the company shall open its principal bank accounts with [bank] and that the bank account signatories shall be the legal representative, the finance officer and any other person authorised by the Board. All payments equal to or exceeding [threshold] shall require two authorised signatures, and the Board ratifies the execution of bank mandate documents under the company seal. RESOLVED, that the Board authorises the engagement of tax advisers, legal counsel and such professional advisers as may be required to complete tax registration, social insurance registration, foreign exchange registration, cybersecurity filings and all statutory post-incorporation obligations. RESOLVED, that the Board adopts the corporate governance policy requiring that material contracts be reviewed by counsel, that all medical-data processing comply with the Personal Information Protection Law, the Data Security Law and the Cybersecurity Law, and that privacy impact assessments be conducted where personal medical data is collected. RESOLVED, that all expenses of incorporation, regulatory licensing and professional advice incurred in the establishment of the company be and are hereby approved as proper corporate expenses, payable upon presentation of invoices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Pre-approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform or the municipal SAMR online name-reservation system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an enterprise name pre-registration application on the competent SAMR online system. The proposed name must follow the statutory structure of administrative division plus distinctive name plus industry characteristic plus limited liability company designation. The applicant must state the proposed business scope, the sole shareholder, the intended legal representative and the prospective registered address. The system checks for prohibited terms, duplicate names, reserved names and trademarks that may create public confusion. For a Hong Kong corporate shareholder, the shareholder's registered Chinese name must appear exactly as in the authenticated corporate documents. No notarisation is required at this stage, but the name-reservation number must be retained and quoted in the subsequent establishment application. If the system flags a conflict, the applicant should promptly file three alternative names.
required_dossiers: Enterprise name pre-registration application form
Basic information of the proposed WFOE and sole shareholder
Proposed business scope and industry description
Authorisation letter for the filing agent
Identity or registration documents of the proposed legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected or suspended on account of duplication or similarity, submit three revised alternative names and request an administrative review by the same SAMR office; the registry will normally release the hold within two working days after the revised submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hong Kong Investor Document Authentication and Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong notary public appointed by the Ministry of Justice of the PRC, acting with the China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited for forwarding and sealing the notarised documents for mainland use
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Hong Kong corporate shareholder must have its corporate records notarised in Hong Kong for use in the PRC. A China-appointed Hong Kong notary public must certify the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, registered office address, register of directors and shareholders, and the corporate resolution authorising the establishment of the WFOE. The notarised package is then transmitted to China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited for sealing and forwarding to the relevant mainland authority. The translated Chinese version of the Articles of Association and the notarised corporate documents must be prepared for submission to SAMR. The Articles of Association should be executed by the sole shareholder and must resolve the capital contribution schedule, governance structure, legal representative, executive director, supervisor, manager, registered address, business scope, allocation of profits and liquidation provisions.
required_dossiers: Hong Kong Certificate of Incorporation
Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate
Certified copy of the Hong Kong registered office address
Register of directors and shareholders
Board resolution of the Hong Kong shareholder authorising the WFOE investment
Passport or identity documents of the ultimate beneficial owner
Notarial certificate issued by the China-appointed Hong Kong notary public
Sealing and forwarding transmission from China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authentication package is returned as deficient, the notary public must supplement the missing pages or exhibits and reseal the dossier through China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited. No substantive resubmission to SAMR is required until the package is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory WFOE Establishment Registration with SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or Provincial Market Supervision Administration in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office, acting under the State Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration with the local Market Supervision Administration, either at the physical government service hall or through the integrated online government service platform. The filing must include the completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company, the Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder, appointment documents for the legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager, the authenticated Hong Kong notarial package, proof of the registered office address and valid identity or registration certificates. The applicant must declare the business scope consistent with the Foreign Investment Negative List and the ISIC 6201 software activities. The authority will review the name, capital, business scope and governance structure, and upon approval will issue the Business License with the Unified Social Credit Code. The statutory registration fee is RMB zero, though small administrative service fees may apply for optional expedited handling.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder
Authentication and notarisation package for the Hong Kong shareholder
Appointment documents for legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager
Proof of registered office address and lease title or landlord consent
Identity cards or passports of the statutory officers
Unified Social Credit Code application data and tax registration questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing to the local Market Supervision Administration within five working days with corrected documents and evidence. If the application is suspended due to negative-list or name concerns, file an administrative reconsideration application or resubmit the corrected dossier after obtaining written clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Compliance Activation, Bank Accounts, Tax, Forex and Cybersecurity Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving enterprise; licensed commercial bank; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); State Taxation Administration and local tax office; public security cybersecurity authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Business License, the WFOE must complete the statutory post-formation steps. It must engrave the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and contract seal at a Public Security Bureau-approved facility and record the seal impressions. The company must open a RMB basic deposit account and, if required, a foreign currency capital account at a licensed bank. The sole shareholder's capital subscription must be contributed in compliance with the Articles of Association and the FDI capital account rules. The company must complete SAFE foreign exchange registration through the delegated bank within the statutory window, complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration, obtain the taxpayer identification number and register payroll, social insurance and housing fund accounts. If the WFOE will process electronic medical records, the company must identify a data protection officer, perform a data security impact assessment, and complete the Cybersecurity Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) classified filing with the local public security authority before production processing of personal medical data begins.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Seal engraving approval certificate from the Public Security Bureau
Bank account opening application and board resolution on bank signatories
FDI foreign exchange registration form and capital contribution statement
Tax registration questionnaire and e-Tax account activation materials
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
Data protection officer appointment and MLPS classification-level filing form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account opening or SAFE registration is delayed due to incomplete beneficial ownership declarations, file the missing ownership chart and supporting corporate records. If MLPS filing is returned for reclassification, engage a certified third-party security assessor to confirm the required protection level and resubmit within the prescribed correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Healthcare Software, Internet Service and Information System Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and provincial Medical Products Administration; Health Commission of the province or municipality; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the WFOE must obtain the sector-specific authorisations required for the EMR SaaS business. If the software qualifies as medical device software under NMPA rules, the company must submit a Class II medical device software registration or filing application, including performance evaluation records, clinical or equivalent validation data, cybersecurity documentation, quality management system evidence and product labelling. If the SaaS is accessed through a website or app in China, the company must complete the ICP Filing or licence with MIIT and, where interactive medical or healthcare advisory functions are present, apply for the Internet Health Information Service qualification with the competent Health Commission. The company must also adopt a service-level and incident-response framework consistent with medical data protection obligations. If the business is purely software hosted in third-party clouds and involves no physical manufacturing, no industrial production licence, EIA permit or fire-safety manufacturing licence is applicable.
required_dossiers: WFOE Business License and Articles of Association
Medical device software classification and intended-use statement
Software validation, verification and cybersecurity testing reports
Quality management system certification or implementation evidence
ICP Filing form and hosting or cloud service agreements
Internet Health Information Service application and clinical safety protocol
Data security, privacy policy and DPIA documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NMPA or Health Commission issues a deficiency query, submit the missing validation and clinical-safety documentation within the stated response window. If the authority suspends the application for insufficient cybersecurity testing, engage an accredited testing institution and resubmit the full dossier without losing prior review credits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and provincial Medical Products Administration; Health Commission of the province or municipality; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP filing and internet information service classification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Software Registration Certificate or Filing Certificate, to the extent the EMR module is regulated as medical device software; Internet Health Information Service Qualification from the Health Commission; ICP Filing from MIIT for internet-hosted SaaS; physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly and warehousing operating licences: Not Applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China and the provincial or municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for the pure cloud-based EMR SaaS operating model with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing; no Full EIA Report or Environmental Registration is required for office-only software activities. If the company later installs on-premises data-centre equipment, server rooms or medical-lab hardware at clinic premises, a separate Environmental Registration and Pollution Permit filing under the MEE classification list would be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC-emitting processes arise from software operations. Office sanitary sewage must comply with local municipal sewer discharge standards where applicable, with general benchmarks such as COD no greater than 500 mg/L, BOD no greater than 300 mg/L and SS no greater than 400 mg/L under GB/T 31962-2015. No flue-gas emission limits apply. End-of-life IT equipment, batteries and electronic waste must be transferred to licensed hazardous or electronic-waste recyclers under the Solid Waste Law of the People's Republic of China.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any occupied office or clinic-integrated server room, the company must obtain the Fire Safety Inspection Certification and operational fire-safety clearance under the PRC Fire Protection Law, including certified fire extinguishers, evacuation signage and emergency lighting. If on-premises server racks or heavy IT infrastructure are installed, a structural load inspection and certification by a licensed structural engineer is required. Occupational safety and health workplace inspection and, where applicable, the workplace safety approval under the PRC Work Safety Law must be completed. In addition, the EMR SaaS processing platform must complete the Cybersecurity Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) classified filing and the associated Level 3 security testing before production use, together with civil-defence and emergency-response documentation appropriate to the physical occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating through the National Electronic Tax Bureau portal at etax.chinatax.gov.cn and the China Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident investor establishing a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) in China must first obtain a business license from the local Market Regulation Administration, which issues the WFOE a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT identification number for the entity under the multi-license integration system. No separate TIN application is required; the tax authority completes the national tax registration automatically within 30 days of the issuance of the business license via inter-agency data sharing. Thereafter, the WFOE legal representative and financial officer must complete biometric real-name authentication on the Electronic Tax Bureau portal, register the entity's bank settlement account for tax payment purposes, file the accounting system and cost-allocation methods, and submit the required anti-fraud compliance declarations for issuance and receipt of electronic invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The WFOE may elect VAT general taxpayer status versus small-scale taxpayer status where eligible under the annual turnover threshold rules. For qualifying cross-border software services, the taxpayer may elect to apply the VAT zero-rating treatment with input VAT credit recovery or the VAT exemption treatment without credit recovery. China does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or hybrid mismatch election under the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 in annual assessable VAT turnover for mandatory general taxpayer registration; however, all WFOEs are unconditionally registered for VAT upon tax registration regardless of turnover since the USCC serves as VAT identification number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Fully digitalized electronic invoices (shu dian piao) are mandatory and must be issued through the national Electronic Invoice Service Platform. The platform transmits complete invoice data to the State Taxation Administration in real time, assigns a unique invoice number, and applies an automatic tax-control stamp or anti-fraud marker. Traditional tax-control disk-based invoicing is no longer required. Every sales invoice, credit note, and related reversal transaction must be cleared through the platform before it is legally valid for input VAT deduction and export zero-rating substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The EMR SaaS and related software services qualify for zero-rated VAT if they are provided to overseas entities and are wholly consumed outside mainland China, meaning the offshore recipient is the party that receives and uses the service, the service is not connected to any domestic sale of goods or transfer of real property, and the intangible service is not used within mainland China. The WFOE must be registered as a VAT general taxpayer, maintain proper records demonstrating the cross-border nature of the transaction, file the zero-rating declaration through the Electronic Tax Bureau, and retain service contracts, invoices, proof of foreign exchange receipt, and if applicable, the offshore service filing record with the tax authority.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) in the qualified form required for physical goods or software media that cross the PRC border, if any part of the EMR SaaS deliverable is shipped as an embedded device or server medium
Cross-Border Service Contract expressly identifying the overseas service recipient, the nature of the EMR SaaS, payment terms, and the place of consumption
Zero-rated VAT invoice issued through the Electronic Invoice Service Platform
Inward Remittance Certificate (Bank Telegraphic Transfer / FIRC equivalent) evidencing receipt of foreign currency from outside mainland China
Bill of Lading or airway bill issued by the carrier for any physical component of the export, where applicable
Proof of login, delivery, or cloud usage by the offshore entity demonstrating that the software service is wholly consumed outside mainland China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The State Taxation Administration may retrospectively disallow export zero-rating claims and claw back all input VAT credits previously refunded, together with statutory late-payment surcharges. Where zero-rating is supported by false documentation, fictitious cross-border service contracts, or unverified foreign exchange receipts, the taxpayer is subject to penalties under Article 63 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law ranging from 50 percent to 500 percent of the unpaid or refunded tax amount. In egregious cases involving fraudulent issuance of zero-rated invoices, the taxpayer may face criminal liability for tax evasion or issuance of false special VAT invoices, including imprisonment, forfeiture of the right to export tax refunds, and public blacklisting in tax integrity records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with current-account convertibility and strict capital-account controls. For a mainland China WFOE with a Hong Kong parent, ordinary operational foreign exchange receipts from SaaS subscriptions are treated as service-trade current-account income and can be credited to a foreign-currency current account or converted into RMB at a designated bank once genuine commercial documents, contracts, and invoices are verified. Export proceeds must be repatriated into mainland China; however, there is no mandatory percentage surrender since SAFE's current-account liberalization reforms. Capital-account transactions, including the injection of registered capital from the Hong Kong parent, require SAFE foreign direct investment registration and the use of a dedicated capital account. Profit remittance to Hong Kong is permitted only after the WFOE has completed statutory annual audit, paid all due taxes, and obtained the bank's verification of distributable reserves; the remittance itself is classified as investment income and enjoys current-account convertibility but still requires the tax payment certificate and audited financial report. The practical treasury design must therefore separate current-account flows, which can be cleared through normal operational accounts, from capital-account flows, which are locked into SAFE-monitored escrow-like accounts until the registered capital is fully verified. Cash-pooling between the WFOE and the Hong Kong parent is not automatic; cross-border intra-group financing must be documented and registered under SAFE rules, and any offshore RMB clearing must comply with the cross-border RMB management framework administered by PBOC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's trade-in-goods monitoring regime, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to mainland China within 180 days after the customs declaration date and must be either credited to the enterprise's foreign-currency current account or settled into RMB at a SAFE-designated bank. There is no statutory percentage of mandatory conversion for export receipts; the converting enterprise may elect to retain the full amount in a foreign-currency account. The settlement bank must verify the export customs declaration, invoice, logistics documents, and the enterprise's trade-facilitation classification before accepting the conversion or credit. For cross-border SaaS and software export proceeds treated as service trade, similar repatriation and declaration duties apply under the International Balance of Payments statistics and SAFE's service-trade monitoring.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (Mainland China branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: SAFE-designated FDI Capital Account for foreign currency registered capital plus RMB Basic Depository Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB settlement and operating account with current-account foreign-currency sub-account
Foreign-currency current-account for export and service-trade receipts plus general RMB operational account
Cross-border RMB settlement account under CIPS and onshore FX hedging margin account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Direct viability is low. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, or Revolut Business are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE as domestic banks and are not permitted to open onshore CNY or foreign-currency clearing accounts, provide SAFE-registered FX settlement, or perform statutory capital verification for a mainland China WFOE. Indirect viability is moderate only when the fintech acts as a front-end receivables or payables facilitator that clears through a fully licensed mainland partner bank or payment institution. Legal constraints require all cross-border FX transactions to be handled by licensed designated forex banks, and foreign EMIs have no standing to register a WFOE's capital-account transactions. The WFOE should therefore maintain its primary treasury and clearing relationships with an onshore Tier-1 commercial bank and use fintech solutions only for invoicing, customer-api orchestration, and reconciliation, never as the legal clearing rail for capital inflows or SAFE-regulated FX settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A newly formed mainland China WFOE cannot rely on remote consular proxy opening for its first corporate account. The statutory legal representative and usually the authorized handler must attend a physical KYC interview at the selected bank branch in person and present the original business license, company chop, articles of association, SAFE FDI registration certificate, and valid passports or national ID cards. If the legal representative is outside China, the bank may require a live video interview in addition to in-person branch attendance by a locally appointed authorized representative holding a notarized power of attorney. Hong Kong corporate documents must be notarized by a China-appointed notary public in Hong Kong and authenticated before submission. Remote electronic KYC alone is generally not accepted by PBOC-regulated banks for a first-time WFOE account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity through a recently incorporated Hong Kong holding company with nominee shareholders and no operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation; registered office service agreement; shareholders register and share certificates; board resolutions appointing the WFOE; UBO declaration and passport copies for all individuals controlling 25 percent or more; full corporate organizational chart from ultimate beneficial owner to the WFOE; audited financial statements or bank reference for the Hong Kong parent for the last two financial years; tax residence certificates; written commercial rationale for the Hong Kong holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-off or non-uniform FDI capital injection from Hong Kong that is inconsistent with the WFOE's projected operating expenses and registered capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: WFOE articles of association and capital contribution schedule; Hong Kong parent board resolution authorizing the transfer; certified bank statements of the remitting Hong Kong account for the preceding six months; source of funds and source of wealth evidence such as dividend income statements, equity sale agreements, or audited profits; SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate with official registration serial number; SWIFT MT103 copy with the correct capital-account payment purpose code; Chinese CPA-issued capital verification report; confirmation that the injection is not funded by unsecured offshore loans masking the ultimate source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring outbound service-trade payments to cloud platforms and overseas sub-processors with low-value, high-frequency patterns that could camouflage trade misinvoicing or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with each cloud or SaaS vendor; detailed monthly invoices and account statements matching payment amounts; purchase orders and service level agreements; SAFE service-trade tax filing certificate or exemption certificate for payments exceeding the relevant USD 50,000 threshold; platform usage and metadata reports; bank payment instructions showing the exact SAFE purpose code; KYB documentation for each vendor; internal transfer-pricing analysis or invoice benchmark.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to U.S. healthcare data and sanctions or export controls due to the medical-clinic EMR SaaS business, increasing financial-crime risk if customers or hosting endpoints are located in restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product security compliance framework and HIPAA business associate agreements; OFAC sanctions screening policy and actual screening reports for customers, users, and endpoints; data residency and geoblocking evidence; export control classification assessment or EAR exemption memo for software and encryption features; restricted-party screening logs; list of banned jurisdictions; board policy on accepting medical clients; third-party penetration test report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound registered capital from the Hong Kong parent must first be booked under SAFE's FDI information registration. The Hong Kong parent should execute a SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated FDI capital account at a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank; field 50K identifies the remitter, field 59 identifies the WFOE beneficiary, and field 70 states FDI registered capital injection with the SAFE registration serial number. The receiving bank performs a compliance check and reports the payment in the international balance of payments statistics. After funds arrive, the WFOE obtains a capital-account confirmation and may apply for foreign-exchange capital settlement into RMB under the capital account for payment of local operating expenses. Each injection is verified by a Chinese certified public accountant, who issues a capital verification report, and the bank will not fully release account controls until capital verification and SAFE filing are closed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EMR software licenses, subscriptions, and third-party cloud services, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 with full remitter and beneficiary details and a valid SAFE service-trade purpose code. For larger clinical IT hardware procurement, a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection can be used through the bank's trade finance desk. Any service-trade outward remittance above the USD 50,000 equivalent must be preceded by a tax filing certificate issued by the tax authority for withholding income tax or VAT on the service fee, unless a tax treaty exemption has been approved. The bank will require the underlying contract, invoice, and proof of the recipient's non-resident status. CIPS can also clear outbound RMB payments to the Hong Kong parent or vendors, and the selected clearing rail depends on the invoice currency and the vendor's settlement capability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD forward contracts with a SAFE-designated bank, permitted only where there is a proven current-account or capital-account underlying exposure and no speculative net positions.
Cross-currency swaps for hedging medium-term foreign-currency debt or registered capital repayment exposure, subject to SAFE registration and real underlying transaction documentation.
Onshore foreign-exchange swaps for temporary liquidity matching between the WFOE's RMB and USD cash flows, supported by cash-flow forecasts and underlying invoices.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards on USD/CNH are not an onshore-clearing vehicle for the mainland WFOE; if the Hong Kong parent needs to hedge CNH/USD balance-sheet exposure, the NDF must be executed outside mainland China by the Hong Kong entity and ring-fenced from the WFOE's operational accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the Hong Kong company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration fee scale from HKD 870 to HKD 3,480 depending on delay; if the return is not delivered within 12 months of the anniversary, the company is liable to prosecution and administrative strike-off by the Registrar, with consequential dissolution and forfeiture of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal before the expiry of the current one-year or three-year business registration certificate; the annual renewal notice must be paid by the expiry date stated on the certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge as prescribed under the Business Registration Ordinance; carrying on business without valid registration is an offence attracting fines and daily penalties, and persistent default may lead to cancellation of the business registration and loss of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Profits Tax Return (BIR51) and Supporting Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the return; electronic filing extensions may apply for returns issued in the April block, subject to the prescribed extension schedule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to HKD 10,000; undercharged profit tax is additionally assessable and may attract penalty up to 3 times the tax undercharged; continued default may result in prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PRC Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Information Report and Enterprise Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June immediately following the calendar year-end, covering the reporting year ended 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file results in inclusion on the Operating Anomaly List and public blacklisting; an administrative fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 30,000 may be imposed, and three consecutive years of non-filing leads to inclusion on the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Filing and Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and local tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the PRC tax year, normally 31 May of the following calendar year for a December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 per return, up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; any underpaid corporate income tax attracts daily overdue interest at 0.05% plus a penalty ranging from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For Hong Kong: a private company must appoint a certified public accountant (practising) to audit its financial statements unless it qualifies for exemption under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The exemption generally applies to a small private company not forming part of a larger group and meeting at least two of three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: annual revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000, total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000, and no more than 100 employees. If any relevant threshold is exceeded for the company or its group, a statutory audit is compulsory. For the PRC WFOE: statutory audit by a PRC-licensed CPA firm is mandatory for every foreign-invested enterprise regardless of turnover, total assets, or headcount; no de minimis audit exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong company: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) or the HKFRS for Private Entities Framework, complying with the Companies Ordinance disclosure requirements. PRC WFOE: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC ASBE / China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS, with additional enterprise income tax adjustments under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong: the Significant Controllers Register (SCR) must be maintained at the registered office or a prescribed location, and any change in significant controller particulars must be recorded within 7 days after notification; the NAR1 Annual Return functions as the annual confirmation of members and shareholding as at the incorporation anniversary. PRC WFOE: any equity transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with SAMR within 30 days after the resolution or transfer instrument, and the annual foreign investment information report must confirm the ultimate beneficial owners and shareholding chain as of 31 December.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charge/Mortgages and Floating Charges
Register of Significant Controllers (UBO Register / SCR)
Statutory Minute Book (Board and Members Resolutions)
Share Transfer Ledger and Capital Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 750 per annum for Hong Kong registered office and company secretary; USD 300 - USD 1,000 per annum for mainland China registered address and annual compliance agent coordination.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,200 - USD 9,500 per annum for combined Hong Kong company audit and PRC WFOE statutory audit, depending on transaction volume, group structure, and EMR SaaS revenue complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard PRC Enterprise Income Tax headline rate is 25%. A qualified software enterprise developing electronic medical record software may access the two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction on taxable income for the first five profitable years after qualifying. A certified High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) is taxed at 15%. Eligible R&D expenses may receive an additional 100% super deduction. Certain encouraged industries in preferential free-trade zones can apply a reduced 15% encouraged-industry rate if the WFOE meets in-zone substantive business and catalogue requirements. General statutory loss carryforward is 5 years; qualified high-tech enterprises and technology SMEs may extend to 10 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Main Form A100000, together with supporting schedules including Schedule A105000, Schedule A105050, Schedule A107012 and the annual related-party transaction disclosure forms, filed through the provincial electronic tax bureau eTax@ChinaTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return plus quarterly prepayment returns; quarterly advance payments are made within 15 days after each quarter-end and the annual return is filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual EIT return must be filed and settled by 31 May of the following year; quarterly prepayment returns are due by 15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January for the immediately preceding quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales and operating revenue from EMR SaaS subscriptions, implementation fees, clinical workflow customisation, data hosting and maintenance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide revenue of the PRC WFOE. If sales are invoiced by a Hong Kong affiliate under a repricing arrangement, identify the related-party flow in the annual TP disclosure and make a compensating adjustment. Reconcile VAT, customs and foreign exchange records with EIT revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, including clinical software engineer salaries, cloud infrastructure, data center hosting, depreciation and amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalise internally developed software under the applicable PRC accounting and tax rules. Claim the R&D super deduction separately. Any cost recharge from a Hong Kong related party must be supported by a fully documented service agreement, actual benefit analysis and arm's length benchmarks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges, including urban maintenance and construction tax and education surcharges based on VAT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Never deduct corporate income tax or VAT itself. Reconcile surcharges with software VAT refund positions. Cross-border medical software services may involve VAT zero-rating or exemption treatment only where export services meet the statutory documentation and contract tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses such as sales commissions, advertising, trade shows and overseas market development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If commissions are paid to a Hong Kong or offshore agent for arranging hospital contracts, apply arm's length rates and document the actual services. Excessive commission margins to a related non-resident can be recharacterised as disguised profit repatriation or taxable service fees requiring withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses including legal, accounting, consulting and group management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PRC EIT law denies a deduction for pure management fees paid to a related party. Only itemised charges for concrete services that confer an economic benefit on the WFOE are deductible. Maintain service contracts, timesheets, deliverables and vendor invoices evidencing cross-border services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, principally interest on shareholder loans, intercompany debt and bank borrowings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest payable to a Hong Kong affiliate is China-source income subject to withholding. Apply the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalisation safe harbor for non-financial enterprises. Interest in excess of the safe harbor may be recharacterised as a dividend and denied deduction. To apply the 7% China-Hong Kong DTA rate, submit a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership evidence before the reduced rate is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and non-operating expenses, including government grants, penalties, deemed dividends and prior-year tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible items such as fines, tax penalties, bribes and expenses without compliant invoices. Non-operating income from a foreign affiliate that in substance is a dividend or royalty must be included and the corresponding WHT position documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after tax law adjustments, tax rate, and final EIT payable after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% standard rate only if no preferential rate is valid. Loss carryforwards must not exceed the statutory period. The annual related-party transaction schedule must be consistent with transfer pricing documentation. Any tax treaty benefit requiring a reduction in WHT on dividends or royalties must be recorded and supported by a valid treaty claim file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers TCAL Article 62 penalties of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increased to RMB 20,000 for serious non-compliance. Unpaid tax accrues a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% under TCAL Article 32. Fraudulent under-declaration is tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, requiring full recovery of tax, a fine from 50% to 500% of the tax evaded, and daily surcharges. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can result in imprisonment up to 7 years plus fines. A legal representative with outstanding tax liabilities may be placed on the tax blacklist and denied exit from China.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% prevailing statutory withholding tax on PRC-source dividends paid by the WFOE to a non-resident corporate shareholder, imposed under EIT Law Articles 3 and 37 and reduced from 20% by Implementation Regulation Article 91. Under the Mainland and Hong Kong SAR Tax Arrangement, the rate is reduced to 5% if the Hong Kong shareholder is the beneficial owner and a company that owns directly at least 25% of the WFOE's shares throughout the 365-day period preceding the dividend payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE as payer must withhold before remitting the dividend. To claim the treaty-reduced 5% rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must file a non-resident treaty benefit claim through the PRC electronic tax bureau, submitting a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department, audited financial statements, board resolutions, a beneficial ownership declaration, group structure chart, proof that the Hong Kong entity has substantive employees, premises, decision-making functions and bank accounts, and evidence that it is not a conduit for shareholders in another jurisdiction. The WFOE must retain all documentation and coordinate with the foreign exchange bank for outbound remittance. If the treaty claim is not approved before remittance, the WFOE must withhold at the statutory 10% rate and the non-resident may apply for a refund. Failure to withhold may make the WFOE liable as withholding agent under EIT Law Article 107.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest to non-residents is 10% of the gross amount. Under the Mainland and Hong Kong SAR Tax Arrangement, interest paid to a Hong Kong beneficial owner is taxed at 7%, and royalties paid to a Hong Kong beneficial owner are taxed at 5%. For EMR software, the character of the payment must be tested: a payment for use of software copyright may be a royalty, whereas a cloud SaaS subscription is generally business profits and becomes taxable in China only through a permanent establishment. Technical and clinical support fees must be separately analysed to prevent recharacterisation as royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB. A Local File is required for the PRC WFOE if annual related-party transactions meet any of these thresholds: tangible asset transfers above RMB 200 million; intangible asset transfers above RMB 100 million; financial asset transfers above RMB 100 million; or other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. A Master File is mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion or when the tax authority specifically issues a notification requiring it.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although the PRC WFOE is a substantive onshore entity and not an offshore vehicle, the anti-abuse doctrines under EIT Law Articles 47 and 48, SAT Public Notice 2017 No. 6, and the China-Hong Kong DTA beneficial ownership tests require that any Hong Kong shareholder, IP holder or service provider actually performs functions, assumes risks and employs personnel for the Core Income-Generating Activities. For an EMR SaaS business, CIGA include software engineering, clinical workflow configuration, data hosting, cybersecurity, contract negotiation, pricing and risk assumption. If those activities are in fact managed and controlled in mainland China while only passive paper documents exist in Hong Kong, the tax authorities will disregard the Hong Kong entity, deny treaty benefits and impose withholding and penal adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and deliberate under-declaration of China-source income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE invoices overseas medical clinics through a Hong Kong marketing vehicle that has no employees, no premises and no business decision-making capacity, while all EMR software development, clinical support, data hosting and contracting are actually performed in mainland China. The Hong Kong vehicle retains a large artificial margin and the PRC entity understates revenue and taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 41 and Article 47 authorise the tax authority to recharacterise the arrangement and make transfer pricing or general anti-avoidance adjustments. TCAL Article 63 classifies deliberate under-declaration as tax evasion, requiring repayment of evaded tax, daily 0.05% late payment surcharge, and a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded. Criminal Law Article 201 imposes imprisonment and fines for large fraudulent tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the directors or de facto controllers abuse the corporate form to divert revenue and evade tax, the PRC Company Law permits piercing the corporate veil, making shareholders and responsible directors jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax, penalties and unpaid corporate creditors. The legal representative can be blacklisted by the tax authority, restricted from leaving China, subjected to asset tracing and civil restitution, and criminally prosecuted with imprisonment up to 7 years for serious evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company DTA abuse and improper treaty relief claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE claims the 5% China-Hong Kong DTA withholding rate on dividends or royalties through a Hong Kong entity that is a bare nominee or conduit: it does not beneficially own the income, has no full-time staff, no physical office, no board minutes and no real economic activity, and simply distributes the funds onward to a third jurisdiction or individual shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SAT Public Notice 2019 No. 35 and the beneficial ownership provisions of the China-Hong Kong Tax Arrangement permit the tax authority to deny treaty benefits and to apply the statutory 10% withholding tax plus late payment surcharge. A false treaty claim may be treated as tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, with penalties of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax. If the WFOE fails to withhold, EIT Law Article 107 makes it liable as the withholding agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false treaty declarations and direct the WFOE to remit dividends without correct withholding expose themselves to personal liability for the unremitted withholding tax, civil asset restitution, travel bans and blacklisting. Criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 may reach 7 years' imprisonment if the false DTA claim forms part of a larger fraudulent underpayment scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and non-arm's length intercompany intellectual property charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays substantial software royalties or technical service fees to a related Hong Kong IP holding company that owns no developed technology, employs no developers and performs no clinical validation, while the WFOE actually incurred the development costs and carries all business risk. No Local File, Master File, contemporaneous benchmarking or annual related-party disclosure is prepared, and the intercompany payments exceed the statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 41 disallows non-arm's length related-party pricing, and Article 44 permits the tax authority to assess taxable income by deemed methods when the taxpayer fails to provide related-party documentation. Interest and late payment surcharges apply under TCAL Article 32 and EIT Law Article 48. TCAL Article 62 imposes administrative fines of RMB 2,000 to RMB 20,000 for failure to maintain records and documentation. In aggravated cases the scheme can be recharacterised as tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement the fictitious IP structure and execute inflated intercompany royalty payments may be found to have siphoned corporate assets through abuse of limited liability, allowing piercing of the corporate veil and joint and several civil liability. Personal consequences include court-ordered restitution, seizure of personal assets, tax blacklisting, travel bans and imprisonment for aiding tax evasion, with sentence length tied to the amount of tax and penalties evaded.
